checks_performed: Compared the exact unrestricted target with the draft's final writeup and coverage claims.
Independently derived the Hilbert–Schmidt decomposition, reconstruction, tensor-moment, purity, conjugation, tensor-product, and extension arguments.

Ran exact_checks.py using only integer cyclotomic arithmetic. It verified the six qutrit candidate rays, their two orthogonal triples, all 30 subgroups of Z_6^2, the 12 order-six isotropic subgroups, and maximum compatible subgroup-family size three.

Ran claim12_exact_checker.py without floating point. It checked both fixed alphabets and the broader vectorwise mixed-alphabet reading, enumerating all 12,288 dephased BH(6,4) bases and all 7,776 dephased sixth-root rays.

claims.claim: For pairwise MUBs, their centered rank-one projectors span mutually orthogonal five-dimensional traceless diagonal subspaces; seven MUBs are equivalent to an orthogonal decomposition of the 35-dimensional traceless Hermitian space into seven such subspaces.
claims.evidence: With P_ki=v_ki v_ki* and Q_ki=P_ki-I/6, direct calculation gives Tr(Q_ki Q_kj)=delta_ij-1/6 and, for k≠l, Tr(Q_ki Q_lj)=0. The within-basis Gram matrix I-J/6 has rank five, and the resulting space is precisely that basis's traceless diagonal space. Seven mutually orthogonal such spaces have dimension 7·5=35 and fill the traceless Hermitian space. Conversely, orthogonality of two such spaces gives Tr(P_ki P_lj)=1/6 for every i,j, which is exactly mutual unbiasedness.
claims.search_method: Direct Hilbert–Schmidt Gram-matrix calculation and dimension count.

claims.claim: Given any six MUBs in C^6, let W be the orthogonal complement of their six centered diagonal subspaces. They extend to a seventh MUB if and only if every pair of matrices in W commutes; if so, the extension is unique.
claims.evidence: The six diagonal spaces are orthogonal and total dimension 30, so dim W=5. An extension has a five-dimensional centered diagonal space contained in W and hence equal to W, proving necessity. Conversely, commuting Hermitian elements of W are simultaneously diagonalizable; since the traceless diagonal space in that eigenbasis also has dimension five, it equals W. Orthogonality then gives squared overlaps 1/6 with each original basis. Adding the identity makes W the full diagonal maximal abelian algebra, whose six minimal rank-one projections are unique, so the extension is unique up to phases and permutation.
claims.search_method: Dimension argument, simultaneous diagonalization, and uniqueness of minimal projections in a maximal diagonal algebra.

claims.claim: A complete set of seven MUBs satisfies the reconstruction identity Σ_ki Tr(AP_ki)P_ki=A+Tr(A)I and the tensor identity Σ_ki P_ki⊗P_ki=I+F.
claims.evidence: Within each centered diagonal space, the six Q_ki have Gram matrix I-J/6 and frame operator equal to that space's identity. Summing over the seven orthogonal spaces reconstructs the traceless part A-Tr(A)I/6. Expanding P_ki=Q_ki+I/6 and using Σ_ki P_ki=7I supplies the scalar part and yields A+Tr(A)I. Pairing this equality with an arbitrary B gives Σ Tr(AP_ki)Tr(BP_ki)=Tr(AB)+Tr(A)Tr(B), exactly the pairing of A⊗B with F+I. Product matrices span the tensor matrix space, proving the tensor identity.
claims.search_method: Tight-frame reconstruction on the seven orthogonal subspaces followed by a nondegenerate tensor-pairing argument.

claims.claim: In a complete set, every unit vector x obeys Σ_ki |⟨x,v_ki⟩|^4=2; a vector unbiased to any chosen six bases must be a ray of the remaining basis.
claims.evidence: Apply claim 2 to P_x and pair with P_x to obtain the fourth-power sum 2. Six unbiased bases contribute 36·(1/6)^2=1. If p_i are the probabilities in the remaining basis, then Σp_i=1 and Σp_i^2=1. Nonnegativity gives Σ_{i≠j}p_i p_j=0, so exactly one p_i is one and all others vanish; x is that basis ray.
claims.search_method: Application of the reconstruction identity and an exact probability-simplex argument.

claims.claim: For any hypothetical complete set and any fixed identification C^6=C^2⊗C^3, the sum of the 42 qubit reduced purities is exactly 30.
claims.evidence: For each P, the swap trick gives Tr[(Tr_B P)^2]=Tr[P⊗P(F_A⊗I_BB)]. Summing and substituting ΣP⊗P=I+F_A⊗F_B gives Tr(F_A)Tr(I_BB)+Tr(I_AA)Tr(F_B)=2·9+4·3=30.

claims.claim: Relative to any fixed C^2⊗C^3 factorization, a complete set contains at most 18 product rays and at most three entirely product bases. Equality forces every other ray to be maximally entangled.
claims.evidence: Every qubit reduction of a bipartite pure state has purity in [1/2,1], with purity one exactly for product rays and purity 1/2 exactly for maximally entangled rays. If P of the 42 rays are product, claim 4 gives 30≥P+(42-P)/2=21+P/2, hence P≤18. Four product bases would give 24 product rays. If P=18, including the case of three product bases, equality holds termwise in the lower bound, forcing all other 24 purities to equal 1/2.
claims.search_method: Sharp reduced-purity bounds combined with the exact total-purity budget.

claims.claim: For any fixed conjugation K, a complete set has at most 12 K-real rays and hence at most two bases consisting entirely of K-real rays.
claims.evidence: Choose orthonormal coordinates in which K is entrywise conjugation and set Ω=Σ_r e_r⊗e_r. Then ⟨Ω,P_v⊗P_v Ω⟩=|Σ_r v_r^2|^2, a number in [0,1] equal to one exactly when the ray is K-real. The tensor identity gives a total of ⟨Ω,(I+F)Ω⟩=2||Ω||^2=12. Thus at most 12 terms can equal one, excluding three all-real six-ray bases.
claims.search_method: Conjugation normal form, equality characterization in Cauchy–Schwarz, and the tensor identity.

claims.claim: Two direct tensor-product bases in C^2⊗C^3 are mutually unbiased if and only if their respective qubit bases and qutrit bases are mutually unbiased.
claims.evidence: Squared product overlaps factor as α_rr'β_ss'. If every product equals 1/6, all factors are positive. Fixing s,s' makes every α_rr' equal; row normalization of the 2×2 local overlap matrix forces α_rr'=1/2. It follows that every β_ss'=1/3. The converse follows immediately by multiplying these local squared overlaps.
claims.search_method: Factorization and row normalization of the two local unistochastic overlap matrices.

claims.claim: Every triple of MUBs in C^3 extends uniquely to four MUBs, and the rays unbiased to all three are exactly the fourth basis.
claims.evidence: Every 3×3 complex Hadamard matrix is equivalent to the Fourier matrix, so the first two bases may be made standard and Fourier. For a dephased flat ray (1,a,b)/sqrt(3), Fourier unbiasedness reduces to a+conj(a)b+conj(b)=0. These are three unit-modulus summands with product one; a zero sum forces them to be the three cube roots, so a,b are cube roots. Exact enumeration then gives precisely (p,q)=(0,1),(0,2),(1,0),(1,1),(2,0),(2,2). The checker verifies that their orthogonality graph has exactly the two triples {(0,1),(1,0),(2,2)} and {(0,2),(1,1),(2,0)}, with every cross-triple squared numerator modulus equal to three. A third basis must be one triple, and exactly the other triple remains unbiased to all three bases.
claims.search_method: Analytic reduction to Z[omega], followed by exhaustive integer enumeration of all nine exponent pairs and their exact orthogonality graph.

claims.claim: If three unit qubit rays form a tight frame with frame operator 3I/2 and are all unbiased to one qubit basis, that basis is the unique qubit basis unbiased to all three rays.
claims.evidence: The three centered projectors lie in the two-dimensional traceless-Hermitian plane orthogonal to the reference basis axis. Tightness makes their sum zero. They cannot span a line: equal-norm vectors in one line would each be ±Q, and an odd sum of three such vectors cannot vanish. Hence they span the full plane. The axis of any qubit basis unbiased to all three rays must lie in the one-dimensional orthogonal complement of this plane, which determines exactly the original unordered basis.
claims.search_method: Bloch-space plane and tight-frame spanning argument.

claims.claim: No maximally entangled vector in C^2⊗C^3 is unbiased to three pairwise MUB direct tensor-product bases.
claims.evidence: Write the bases as A_k⊗B_k. For a maximally entangled ψ, its qutrit reduction is Π_S/2. Summing the assumed probabilities 1/6 over the two A_k outcomes gives ⟨b,Π_S b⟩=2/3 for every b in each B_k. Thus the ray w=S-perp is unbiased to B_1,B_2,B_3 and, by claim 8, is in their unique fourth basis B_4. If c_0,c_1 are the other B_4 rays, Schmidt form gives ψ=(a_0⊗c_0+a_1⊗c_1)/sqrt(2). For each fixed k, the three normalized conditional qubit rays obtained from b∈B_k are all unbiased to {a_0,a_1}, have frame operator 3I/2, and the uniform product probabilities make them unbiased to A_k. Claim 9 therefore forces every A_k={a_0,a_1}, contradicting their pairwise mutual unbiasedness from claim 7.
claims.search_method: Reduced-state projection argument, the qutrit completion classification, and exact conditional-frame normalization.

claims.claim: A complete seven-MUB set in C^2⊗C^3 cannot contain three direct tensor-product bases; consequently it contains at most two such bases.
claims.evidence: Three direct tensor-product bases supply 18 product rays. Claim 5 then forces every ray in the remaining four bases to be maximally entangled. Each of those rays would be unbiased to all three product bases, contradicting claim 10. Hence three such bases are impossible.
claims.search_method: Combination of the sharp purity-equality case with the maximally-entangled-vector obstruction.

claims.claim: If one basis is standard and every vector in every other basis has coordinates consisting entirely of fourth roots, or entirely of sixth roots, divided by √6, then the MUB family has at most two bases.
claims.evidence: For two fourth-root rays an unbiased overlap would require A^2+B^2=6, impossible modulo three. For two sixth-root rays it would require A^2+AB+B^2=6; parity forces A,B even and hence divisibility by four, also impossible. This proves the fixed-alphabet cases and implies, under the broader vectorwise reading, that two nonstandard bases would have to be respectively entirely fourth-root and entirely sixth-root. The exact checker closes that omitted mixed case: it normalizes one BH(6,4) column to all ones, exhausts the 72 normalized orthogonality cliques and all row-phase shifts to obtain all 12,288 dephased BH(6,4) bases, and tests all 7,776 dephased sixth-root rays using integral Q(zeta_12) coordinates. The maximum number of sixth-root rays unbiased to any such basis is zero. Thus no two nonstandard bases exist under either reading.
claims.search_method: Modular obstruction plus complete exact enumeration in Z[i], Z[zeta_6], and Q(zeta_12); no floating-point decisions.

claims.claim: For the standard dimension-six Weyl construction, order-six isotropic subgroups L≤Z_6^2 give stabilizer bases, and two such bases are mutually unbiased exactly when their label subgroups intersect only at zero.
claims.evidence: The Weyl matrices X^aZ^b are Hilbert–Schmidt orthogonal and commute exactly when their label symplectic product vanishes modulo six. An order-six isotropic subgroup therefore spans a six-dimensional commutative star-subalgebra of M_6. Such an algebra has six nonzero minimal projections whose ranks sum to six, so all are rank one and form its joint eigenbasis. Its traceless part is spanned by the five nonidentity Weyl labels. Two such parts are orthogonal exactly when their nonzero label sets are disjoint, equivalently L∩M={0}; centered-projector orthogonality is exactly mutual unbiasedness. The checker independently generates all subgroups and confirms the 12 order-six cases are isotropic.
claims.search_method: Weyl commutator and finite-dimensional star-algebra proof, with exhaustive exact subgroup generation as a check.

claims.claim: At most three pairwise MUB stabilizer bases arise from the dimension-six Weyl construction, and three are attainable.
claims.evidence: Every order-six subgroup contains a nonzero element of order two. Z_6^2 has exactly three nonzero involutions: (3,0),(0,3),(3,3). Pairwise-trivially-intersecting subgroups must contain distinct involutions, giving the upper bound three. The horizontal, vertical, and diagonal cyclic subgroups are order-six isotropic subgroups with pairwise intersection {0}, attaining the bound. Exact generation of all 30 subgroups and clique search over the 12 order-six isotropic subgroups independently returns maximum three.
claims.search_method: Involution pigeonhole argument, explicit construction, and exhaustive integer subgroup/clique enumeration.

target_evidence: The exact target requires either an unrestricted proof that seven MUBs in C^6 do not exist or an exact construction of seven bases with every identity verified. The draft supplies neither: it explicitly leaves the unrestricted decomposition with arbitrary phases and non-stabilizer structure open. Its verified structural identities and exclusions of product, real, restricted-phase, and Weyl-stabilizer subclasses are material but incomplete progress, and the final writeup expressly says so. Therefore target coverage is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS, and the draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is ACCURATE rather than overstated or understated.
